definitions.gloss: to put forth, to announce, to launch (a policy/plan)
definitions.explanation: To publicly announce or introduce a new policy, plan, or initiative. Often used for official or organizational announcements.
To shape metal by hammering from the inside to create a raised pattern on the outside.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{方針|ほうしん}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To put forth a new policy.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}が{新|あたら}しい{経済|けいざい}{政策|せいさく}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The government put forth a new economic policy.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{環境|かんきょう}{対策|たいさく}の{方針|ほうしん}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}している。
examples.english: The company is putting forth its environmental policy.

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}が{銅板|どうばん}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}して{模様|もよう}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: The craftsman hammers out the copper plate to create a pattern.

examples.japanese: {金属|きんぞく}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}して{装飾品|そうしょくひん}を{作|つく}る{技術|ぎじゅつ}は{古|ふる}くからある。
examples.english: The technique of hammering out metal to make ornaments has existed since ancient times.

examples.japanese: {革|かわ}に{模様|もよう}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To emboss a pattern on leather.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive).

COMPOUND VERB: Formed from {打|う}つ (to strike) + {出|だ}す (to put out). The combination creates the meaning of 'bringing something forth by striking' or metaphorically 'putting something forward publicly.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{政策|せいさく}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す (put forth a policy)
・{方針|ほうしん}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す (announce a policy direction)
・{対策|たいさく}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す (launch countermeasures)
・{姿勢|しせい}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す (show one's stance)

USAGE: Sense 1 is far more common in modern Japanese, frequently appearing in news and business contexts.
